Class TimedEffect

java.lang.Object
net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.TimedEffect
All Implemented Interfaces:
IChromaticEffect
public final class TimedEffect extends Object implements IChromaticEffect
Changes animation playback speed without changing the wrapped effect's geometry controls.

The foreground color, scale and offset methods multiply the current animation time by this wrapper's speed before calling the underlying effect. That effect reads the adjusted time from TextEffectClock.milliseconds(). The caller's clock is restored after the sample, even if the callback throws. A speed of 0.5 plays at half speed, zero holds the initial phase, and negative speed runs time backward.

Direct calls to getOpacity(), getOutlineColor() and capability flags delegate without opening a time scope. They see the caller's current clock. The native renderer instead unwraps the effect with base(IChromaticEffect) and opens one open(IChromaticEffect) scope around its glyph samples. Calls to that base object, including opacity, then see the adjusted time.

When sampling manually, use either the wrapper's methods or the base object inside an open scope. Calling the wrapper inside its own scope applies the multiplier again: half speed becomes quarter speed.

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static IChromaticEffect of(IChromaticEffect effect, double speed)
      Returns an effect with a separate playback multiplier, collapsing an existing wrapper when needed.

      Rate one returns the supplied object unchanged. Other nested rates multiply before validation; a resulting rate of one returns the unwrapped base object. Wrapping an existing half-speed effect with another rate of 0.5 therefore produces quarter speed; it does not replace the earlier rate.

      Parameters:
      effect - non-null shared callback to wrap
      speed - finite playback multiplier; combined rates must be within -32 through 32
      Returns:
      original, unwrapped or wrapped effect as described above
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if effect is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the combined playback multiplier is nonfinite or outside the bounds

    • open

      public static TextEffectClock.Scope open(IChromaticEffect effect)
      Opens this effect's playback scope using the caller's currently visible animation time.

      Inside the scope, sample base(effect) to avoid applying this rate a second time. For example, a rate of 0.5 inside a caller scope at 1000 milliseconds exposes 500 milliseconds. Another open of the same effect inside that scope exposes 250. Closing each scope restores its parent's time.

      An ordinary effect or null uses rate one but still opens a new frozen-time scope. This method does not mutate the effect or change another thread's clock.

      Parameters:
      effect - wrapped or ordinary effect, or null for an unchanged clock rate
      Returns:
      scope that must close on this thread in reverse nesting order
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if multiplied time is not finite

    • getRenderColor

      public int getRenderColor(int color, float x, float y)
      Samples the glyph color at this playback speed, then restores the caller's clock. Chooses the color for the current glyph sample.

      The renderer can sample multiple corners to create a gradient. Return the input color when this effect should leave it unchanged. Supply transparency through IChromaticEffect.getOpacity(); alpha bits in the returned color are ignored.

      Specified by:
      getRenderColor in interface IChromaticEffect
      Parameters:
      color - incoming packed RGB color
      x - horizontal sample position in GUI pixels
      y - vertical sample position in GUI pixels
      Returns:
      packed RGB color from the wrapped effect

      public float getScale(float x, float y)

    • transformsWholeSegment

      public boolean transformsWholeSegment()
      Returns the wrapped effect's transform scope without changing the clock. Selects one transform for the whole consecutive run instead of a transform per letter.

      A segment is a run sharing an effect identity and its relevant outline state. Whole-segment transforms use one center and preserve the run's nominal layout width: a breathing word can grow visually without pushing the next word back and forth.

      Specified by:
      transformsWholeSegment in interface IChromaticEffect
      Returns:
      whether the wrapped effect transforms a whole segment at once
